learner_operation: Use Gaussian elimination on a singular two-equation, two-variable system; distinguish a contradictory final row from a redundant row and select the complete general solution.

fixed_features.feature: Two equations in x,y with singular rank-one coefficient matrix and an x-first pivot
fixed_features.justification: Target KP title, canonical example 681fce57-6be7-5907-b575-8c34b4819ae5, and lesson 3153 teach this elimination and free-variable structure.

fixed_features.feature: Easy first x coefficient equals 1; one elimination operation
fixed_features.justification: Every easy practice source has this workload; moderate sources additionally normalize the pivot.

fixed_features.feature: One five-option radio field, including No solution and four complete vector forms
fixed_features.justification: All 17 captured practice questions use this response contract. Canonical example lacks a bank and is not assigned an invented one.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Hold coefficients and first RHS fixed; choose second RHS either proportional or nonproportional. Derive final row, classification, explanation, and key.
answer_roles.observed: Unjustifiably fixed per source profile. A common nonzero scaling cannot change consistency. Every recognizable coefficient signature preserves one classification.

answer_roles.role: Surviving affine intercept and y slope
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Vary first RHS independently including zero; vary coefficient slope within same easy elimination method.
answer_roles.observed: Only signed nonzero multiples of original nonzero intercepts occur. Slopes are fixed; zero-intercept source q-20964 is absent.

answer_roles.role: Correct bank member and displayed position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Recompute correct vector/text answer from the actual system. UI position may vary without changing semantics.
answer_roles.observed: Correct member fixed within stored profile; actual UI shuffles display order. The finding concerns coefficient-to-action dependency, not stored-index repetition.

coverage.result: Raw easy domain has 32 dependent-consistent and 32 inconsistent records. Shared delivery removes one source replay per profile, leaving 28 of each; all 8 profiles remain outcome-fixed.
5/5 survive: 3 consistent, 2 inconsistent; only four profiles, with q-20783 represented by opposite-sign RHS scales. The shortcut succeeds on every delivered member.
q-20964 (897c434c-2b3e-570b-8210-f27b51719e55), x-5y=0; 2x-10y=3, cannot replay. 16 other complete banks and corrected solution sequences replay.

Internal mathematical-fingerprint dedup retains 64 easy records; delivery retains 56. Selection only chooses a fresh candidate in a weighted band, so it cannot break the per-record shortcut. 192 concrete easy-only fixture draws preserve it.

counterfactuals.change: q-73750: hold coefficients fixed, scale both RHS values from t=1 to t=2.
counterfactuals.expected: General solution intercept changes from 4 to 8; y slope remains +2. Prompt, matrices, solved x, vector bank/key and grading must agree.
counterfactuals.observed: Both instances independently solve to x=4+2y and x=8+2y; actual grader accepts each own correct choice and rejects all alternatives; actual UI shows the changed constants and solution.
counterfactuals.justification: Lesson 3153 derives the basic-variable intercept from the remaining first equation.

counterfactuals.change: Hold x-6y=2 and second coefficients -4x+24y fixed; change only second RHS from -10 to -8.
counterfactuals.expected: No solution changes to x=2+6y, y free; the zero final row replaces a contradiction, and No solution must be rejected.
counterfactuals.observed: Independently authored expected fixture passes exact math, actual native grading, and actual UI rendering. Current generator cannot produce the changed role: all eight allowed q-42157 scales are inconsistent. Strict regression exits 1. Expected fixture is not claimed as current generator output.
counterfactuals.justification: Tutorials 3901 and 3154 explicitly base inconsistency on a nonzero eliminated RHS, not on coefficient labels or template membership.

counterfactuals.change: Within inconsistent q-42157, double both RHS values using t=1 -> t=2, retaining a nonzero contradiction.
counterfactuals.expected: Eliminated RHS changes -2 -> -4 but response remains No solution; explanation and matrices must reflect the new residual.
counterfactuals.observed: Independently checked echelon rows are [0,0,-2] and [0,0,-4]. Both actual native keys accept No solution and reject every vector; rendered prompts and explanations show the corresponding constants.
counterfactuals.justification: Tutorial 3901 explains that any nonzero RHS in 0=d is false. Residual magnitude within the nonzero branch does not affect the requested solution.

shortcut_probes.cue: Visible coefficient signature; ignore RHS for consistency
shortcut_probes.subgroup: scale=1-trained lookup tested on all other scales
shortcut_probes.strategy: For known inconsistent coefficient signatures select No solution; for consistent signatures choose the vector satisfying only the first equation, ignoring the second.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is uniform selection among five radio options. Coefficients alone cannot determine consistency mathematically; learned signatures nevertheless predict the answer-producing action on every held-out scale. Solving the first row on the consistent branch is legitimate partial work but bypasses the essential consistency check.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Visible coefficient signature predicts No solution for q-73749 and q-42163. For q-73750 and q-20783, ignore second equation and select the vector satisfying the first equation. All five native correct choices found; independent of UI choice order.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is 1/5 random radio selection. Two records select No solution by signature; three solve only the first equation after using the signature to assume consistency. All five survive the actual filter; larger controls cannot waive this batch failure.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose the displayed option at the stored correct index
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is 1/5 random selection. Actual learning.js hashes item/field/choice IDs to reorder choices; fixed stored position is rejected as an independent learner-facing finding.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose No solution without reading either RHS
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is uniform choice among five answers. Coefficient signature fixes consistency and the associated action on all eight scales, including seven held-out scales. For this rank-one family a different second RHS can require the opposite classification with the same coefficients; source-example membership does not justify fixing that role.

delivery.result: Shortcuts survive every examined stage. Easy domain 64 -> 56; exact batch 5 -> 5. For coefficient -6, choose No solution remains correct for 7/7 delivered variants. Selection is a subset operation, so no unknown learner history or weights can repair the dependency within the generated pool. All 17 captured inventory records are original sources; no stored generated instances were found.

limitations: Captured inventory is math basis 5364; later concurrent changes are not examined.

Live policy weights, learner histories, and future database entity IDs are absent. Selection fixture draws use explicit easy-only weights and fixture IDs, while the dependency conclusion holds for all nonempty fresh subsets. No live selection frequency is claimed.
The canonical example has no answer fields; no canonical bank is invented.
The expected consistency-changing pair is independently authored review evidence, not current generator output.
Finite-domain checks and simple cue probes do not establish absence of every possible shortcut.
